title: Arrow interoperability in `mizu_map()`
description:
Reported by a user:

> Sending an Arrow table through mizu_channel() works in a fresh R session, but after calling mizu_collect() on a mizu_map() result, the same operation fails with:
Error: attempt to apply non-function
After investigating the C source, I found a possible initialization-order bug in src/arrow.c. The arrow_ns() function checks whether MIZU_PRIV_MIZU_NS is initialized, but that slot can already be populated by verbs_pool.c, leaving the Arrow-specific function references uninitialized.
A potential fix would be to change the initialization guard from:
MIZU_PRIV_MIZU_NS
to:
MIZU_PRIV_FN_ARROW_NS
I'm running R 4.6.0, mizu 0.1.0, Arrow 25.0.1, and Nanoarrow 0.9.0 on Linux.

title: Release mizu 0.1.0
description:
Prepare for release:

* [x] `git pull`
* [x] Check [current CRAN check results](https://cran.rstudio.org/web/checks/check_results_mizu.html)
* [x] [Polish NEWS](https://style.tidyverse.org/news.html#news-release)
* [x] `urlchecker::url_check()`
* [x] `devtools::build_readme()`
* [x] `devtools::check(remote = TRUE, manual = TRUE)`
* [x] `devtools::check_win_devel()`
* [x] Update `cran-comments.md`
* [x] `git push`
* [x] Draft blog post

Submit to CRAN:

* [x] `usethis::use_version('minor')`
* [x] `devtools::submit_cran()`
* [x] Approve email

Wait for CRAN...

* [x] Accepted :tada:
* [x] Finish & publish blog post
* [ ] Add link to blog post in pkgdown news menu
* [x] `usethis::use_github_release()`
* [x] `usethis::use_dev_version(push = TRUE)`
* [ ] Share on social media
* [ ] Slack link to blog post, bluesky, and linkedin in #open-source-comms

title: Streaming map

title: Should common arguments be dot-prefixed
description:
From @topepo:

> Is there a reason to have different argument names for common parameters between mirai_map() and mizu_map()? For example, mirai_map(.x, .f, .args) and mizu_map(x, f).
